theme: Kaggle-style Airbnb listing snapshot datasets committed to GitHub (any city, any year), especially multi-year or multi-city collections
queries_run: gh search repos: airbnb dataset multi-city
gh search repos: airbnb listings csv (sort updated)
gh search repos: airbnb price prediction dataset
gh search repos: airbnb europe cities dataset
gh search repos: inside airbnb archive
gh search repos: airbnb open data (403 rate-limited on second query in same call, airbnb-dataset topic)
WebSearch: site:github.com airbnb multi-city dataset europe listings csv repository
WebSearch: site:github.com "inside airbnb" archive mirror historical dumps 2015..2022
WebSearch: site:github.com airbnb listings.csv calendar.csv multiple cities repository dataset -tutorial
WebSearch: github repository airbnb dataset South America OR Asia listings prices scraped multiple years

candidates.name: OludolapoAnalyst/AirBnB
candidates.what_it_holds: The well-known 'Airbnb Prices in European Cities' collection: 10 European cities (Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, London, Paris, Rome, Vienna), each with a *_weekdays.csv and *_weekends.csv file (20 CSVs total). Fields include price, room type, superhost status, amenity counts, distance to center, attraction/restaurant indices. Original source scrape circa 2018-19, CC0 licensed. This repo re-hosts/re-packages it for a SQL+PowerBI project.
candidates.why_useful: Multi-city European snapshot with a weekday/weekend price split not present in our Inside Airbnb panel (which has no Rome/Paris/London day-of-week price granularity for that vintage); useful as an older cross-section comparator for European ADR levels/gap 1 (older archived data) and gap 20 (day-of-week demand pattern proxy).
candidates.size_hint: 20 CSV files, city-level listing counts (hundreds-thousands/city typical of this Kaggle dataset)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying source data as widely-mirrored 'Airbnb Prices in European Cities' Kaggle set; not identical to our held 13-city Inside Airbnb panel (different cities: Athens, Budapest, Vienna, Berlin not all in our panel) or vintage (pre-Dec-2022).

candidates.name: silent-j/Airbnb-Data-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Six committed CSVs (in datasets.zip) for three Spanish cities: barcelona_list.csv, madrid_list.csv, valencia_list.csv (listing/property features) plus barcelona_cal.csv, madrid_cal.csv, valencia_cal.csv (calendar: listing id x date x availability x PRICE for the 12 months forward from Sep 2019). Downloaded directly from insideairbnb.com on 2019-09-18.
candidates.why_useful: A pre-2023 Inside Airbnb calendar snapshot WITH price data for Madrid/Valencia (not in our 13-city panel) and an older Barcelona vintage than we hold; directly fills gap 1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023) and is one of the few sources with realized forward calendar pricing from that era.
candidates.time_coverage: Snapshot taken 18 Sep 2019; calendar covers ~Sep 2019-Oct 2020 forward-looking
candidates.size_hint: 6 CSVs, city listing counts each likely 10k-20k rows (typical Inside Airbnb city size at that date) plus 365-day calendar per listing
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Older/finer than our held Inside Airbnb 13-city panel (Dec-2022 onward) and older than our 2024-25 calendar vintages; Madrid/Valencia are new geographies for us.

candidates.name: tmasjc/airbnb-market-data
candidates.what_it_holds: R/Shiny app that ships small starter listings.csv for Berlin and Vienna, plus a command-line tool (download_csv.R) that pulls InsideAirbnb 'listings.csv' summary files for 30+ cities on demand; README references Vienna snapshots reaching back to at least March 2017.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made client for pulling InsideAirbnb historical snapshots (potentially including vintages no longer on the live CDN, which currently keeps only ~1 year); worth checking whether its URL list/date index reaches further back than our current archive, which would fill gap 1.
candidates.time_coverage: at least back to March 2017 for some cities, per README
candidates.size_hint: small starter CSVs bundled; full pulls on demand are InsideAirbnb-scale (10k-100k rows/city)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our existing InsideAirbnb holdings in mechanism, but its download tool/URL list may reach older vintages than our current 168-dump archive.

candidates.name: urbanbigdatacentre/ubdc-airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Containerized, continuously-running scraper (University of Glasgow Urban Big Data Centre) that hits airbnb.com directly for user-defined geographic areas, collecting listing details, calendar availability, booking policies, host info, and reviews; per web coverage it has been running daily since 2020. Data is stored externally in a PostGIS/PostgreSQL database, not committed to the repo. A related dataset appears at researchdata.gla.ac.uk/2056 ('Airbnb raw scraped data collection').
candidates.why_useful: If the associated Glasgow research-data deposit (external, non-GitHub) holds pre-built daily-since-2020 calendar/booking data across many cities, it would be a strong candidate for realized occupancy/booking-lead-time proxies (gaps 2, 3). Flagging the METHOD only, per repo instructions: scraper directly hits airbnb.com — CLAUDE.md rule 6 says any scrape beyond Inside Airbnb/the sanctioned fee-panel is a ToS decision for a human; do not run this.
candidates.geography: user-configurable, per published UBDC studies has covered UK and other cities
candidates.size_hint: unknown; 58 commits on repo, external DB not sized
candidates.last_activity: unknown, active project with devcontainer/CI configs
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Different mechanism from our Inside Airbnb holdings (continuous first-party scrape of airbnb.com vs. Inside Airbnb's periodic public dumps); the external Glasgow data deposit (researchdata.gla.ac.uk/2056) may itself be a stored dataset worth a follow-up look outside GitHub.

candidates.name: airbert-vln/bnb-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Scripts (MIT licensed) that scrape airbnb.com listings/photos/captions across cities pulled from Wikipedia place lists, for a vision-language-navigation research paper; pre-computed TSV files (listing id, photo id, image URL, caption, visual features) are committed for a dataset generated 'Christmas 2019'; the full LMDB image database is NOT shareable (Airbnb IP restriction).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal for KPI forecasting -- it is an image/caption dataset for ML vision research, not pricing/occupancy/nights data. Listed for completeness since it is a real, non-trivial airbnb.com-derived academic dataset with committed files, but it doesn't bear on any numbered gap directly.
candidates.geography: cities drawn from Wikipedia place listings, global, unspecified count
candidates.size_hint: pre-computed TSVs committed; scale not stated in README
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: No overlap with anything we hold; distinct modality (images/captions, not price/occupancy).

candidates.name: msr-ds3/airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Academic (Data Science Summer School / MSR-DS3) project titled 'Airbnb: Predicting Loyalty' with a committed raw_data folder, load_historical_data.R, and exploration/historical_exploration scripts (e.g. lou_listings_history_amenities.R, suggesting a Louisville, KY panel) analyzing host/guest return behavior over time using Inside Airbnb history; 280 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Possible longitudinal (multi-snapshot-over-time) Inside Airbnb panel for a city (Louisville) outside our current 13-city set, with host/guest repeat-booking features that could proxy loyalty/retention dynamics; needs a directory listing to confirm exact vintages/row counts before treating as more than a lead.
candidates.geography: Louisville, KY (inferred from file naming) plus possibly other cities
candidates.last_activity: unknown (280 commits, academic project, likely dated ~2018-2019 DS3 cohort)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Possibly a new city (Louisville) not in our panel; unconfirmed overlap otherwise.

candidates.name: isammitr/airbnb-amsterdam
candidates.what_it_holds: Amsterdam-specific Inside Airbnb export: listings.csv, calendar.csv, reviews.csv used for price prediction and peak-season analysis.
candidates.why_useful: Single-city, single-vintage Amsterdam snapshot; only useful if its vintage predates our current CDN-limited coverage (Amsterdam is outside our 13-city panel entirely), so it is a new geography at minimum.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Amsterdam is not in our held 13-city Inside Airbnb panel, so this is a new geography even as a single snapshot.

candidates.name: dsbb1234/AirBnB-Seattle-and-Boston
candidates.what_it_holds: The classic 2016 Airbnb-published Seattle + Boston open dataset (listings, calendar, reviews for both cities), used to compare host vs superhost behavior.
candidates.why_useful: Two US cities (Seattle, Boston) not in our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel, from a 2016 vintage -- older than anything we hold and a different original source (Airbnb's own 2016 Kaggle release, not Inside Airbnb), directly relevant to gap 1 (older archived dumps).
candidates.size_hint: listings/calendar/reviews CSVs per city, Kaggle-scale (few thousand listings each)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: New cities and an older (2016) vintage than anything in our current panel; this is the commonly-mirrored 2016 Airbnb Seattle/Boston Kaggle set, so many equivalent mirrors exist on GitHub.

candidates.name: harshadagrawal/Rio-de-janeiro-Airbnb-open-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Rio de Janeiro Inside Airbnb open-data export used for an analysis notebook; single city, likely single vintage.
candidates.why_useful: LatAm geography (Rio) not in our 13-city panel (we hold Mexico City only for LatAm); worth a quick check for vintage/fields, could add a second LatAm data point relevant to gap 7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) indirectly via STR supply.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: New LatAm city (Rio) beyond our held Mexico City coverage.

candidates.name: Hari-2782/Airbnb-Data-Warehouse-BI-Solution
candidates.what_it_holds: SQL Server/SSIS BI project built on 'Airbnb Open Data' (the well-known NYC-based Kaggle set with extra fields like host verification, cancellation policy, house rules); MIT licensed, 9 stars, most-starred repo found for generic 'airbnb open data' search.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal -- appears to be the standard single-city NYC Kaggle file with a BI wrapper. Flagged only because it is the highest-starred hit and includes a cancellation_policy field, which is tangential to the RNPL/cancellation-rate thesis (gap 3) if the underlying columns hold real cancellation-policy distributions rather than just the policy label.
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified NYC Airbnb Open Data vintage
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Likely duplicates the standard NYC Kaggle file already excluded by scope rules; flagged only for the cancellation_policy field angle, otherwise should be treated as excluded boilerplate.

notes: gh search repos is extremely noisy for this theme: the vast majority of hits are single-notebook re-analyses of the canonical AB_NYC_2019.csv or the 2016 Seattle/Boston Kaggle file with no new data -- excluded per instructions. Hit a 403 rate-limit on the 7th gh search call (two gh invocations in one Bash call); switched to WebSearch + WebFetch for the remainder as instructed, which surfaced more useful multi-city collections (European weekday/weekend set, Spain calendar-with-price archive) that gh's repo-search text index does not rank well because their READMEs don't repeat 'airbnb dataset' keywords. The single highest-value lead is NOT a GitHub-native dataset: Urban Big Data Centre's continuous airbnb.com scrape (ubdc-airbnb, method only, external PostGIS store) and its companion Glasgow research-data deposit (researchdata.gla.ac.uk/2056, outside GitHub, not fetched) could plausibly hold multi-year daily calendar/booking panels across cities since 2020 -- worth a dedicated non-GitHub scout follow-up, and any use of the scraper itself is a ToS question per CLAUDE.md rule 6, not something to run. Did not attempt gh api directory-listing calls (budget consumed by search calls before confirming any repo needed one); WebFetch summaries above are unverified against actual file listings and should be spot-checked with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/` before citing exact row counts in a memo.
